summary: Get emergency care now—call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department, and sort out the cost afterward. This estimate uses Aetna's negotiated rate and covers the hospital's bill only; the emergency physician bills separately, and that bill is not included. The visit level is assigned after care, so the actual hospital bill may differ.
ifAdmitted: If formally admitted as an inpatient, the estimate lists a patient share of $5,000 for the chest-pain admission, billed as one case rate under inpatient benefits. An overnight stay under observation is outpatient care billed service by service, so it is different from inpatient admission and the admission estimate may not apply. Ask the care team which status applies.
drivers:
A lower visit level with expected tests could mean a lower share; a higher level or possible tests could raise it.
A possible chest CT angiogram is one of the larger estimated items.
The estimate says observation is possible and admission is possible; these can change how the hospital bills the stay.
questions:
Is my dad under observation or formally admitted as an inpatient?
Which tests are included in the hospital estimate, and which possible tests were not included in the typical amount?
What will Aetna count toward the deductible and out-of-pocket maximum for this hospital visit?
Will the emergency physician send a separate bill, and how can we check its coverage?
rights:
The emergency department must provide a medical screening exam and stabilizing treatment regardless of ability to pay or insurance.
He can ask the care team whether he is formally admitted or under observation.
basis: Used Aetna’s negotiated hospital rates for the ED estimate and the admission and observation pricing, since Aetna is listed and matches the stated insurer.
assumptions:
Adult patient, age 58
No additional symptoms or medical history provided
